scout.title: Scout Architecture
scout.subtitle: Adaptive municipal discovery and semantic compilation
scout.story: Swiss municipalities are heterogeneous. Scout uses AI to adapt its search strategy and to understand how each municipality handles its services, then compiles that heterogeneity into one stable municipality contract for the MCP Factory.

principle.title: Scout does not build the MCP server.
principle.text: Scout understands heterogeneous municipal reality and compiles it into one stable municipality contract.

inputs.name: Municipality URL
inputs.summary: Validated before the first request: public http(s) only, non-global IPs rejected, redirects re-checked. Same guarantees in Agent Scrap and the older prototype.
inputs.next: Add BFS number to the municipality identity.

inputs.name: Service Index
inputs.desc: Known service concepts Scout actively looks for.
bullets: Scout may suggest variants and new services — never edits the index itself
inputs.summary: service-index/v1, version mvp-1: five entries — waste_collection, move_in, office_hours, forms, building_application — with German labels and synonyms. Patrick's plan standardizes 7 services, and the grounding matrix tracks 32 tools.
inputs.next: Align the index with the Factory's 7 standard services.

cards.name: Recon
cards.desc: Inspect site shape, language, structure, portals.
cards.summary: Fetches the homepage and records title, language, internal link count, sampled links and service-directory candidates (dienstleistung, online-schalter, guichet, sportello). No sitemap, CMS, portal or site-size probe yet.
cards.next: Add sitemap + CMS fingerprint so Dübendorf is recognised as a directory site.

cards.name: Choose strategy
cards.desc: A typed, bounded plan: mode, reason, roots, budgets.
cards.summary: A PydanticAI Strategy Agent returns a typed ScoutStrategy from the recon result; without a model a heuristic picks it (≤80 links and no directory → broad, else targeted). Heuristic path tested; the agent path has not been run against a live model.
cards.next: Run the agent path on the five benchmark sites.

cards.name: Scouting strategy
cards.summary: Two modes run: broad_small_site and a generic `targeted` (the docs call it targeted_large_city). service_directory and mixed_content are not implemented yet.

cards.name: Discover services
cards.desc: Find indexed services; notice possible new or variant ones.
cards.summary: Pages are matched against Service Index labels and synonyms; unmatched service-like pages become possible_new catalog suggestions. `variant` exists in the contract but is never emitted.
cards.next: Emit variant when a page matches an indexed service with a local twist.

cards.name: Source bundles
cards.desc: Group the official material behind one service.
cards.summary: Each service keeps its forms, PDFs and official handoffs with Scout source roles. Real Binn finding: strahlerpatente.binn.ch is kept as an official_handoff on a municipality-owned sibling subdomain without being crawled (tested).
cards.next: Add contact pages and structured feeds to the bundle.

cards.name: Semantic service inspection
cards.desc: What service is this? How is it handled here?
cards.summary: A PydanticAI Service Inspector returns a typed ServiceInterpretation per finding; without a model a keyword heuristic stands in. The agent path has never been run against a live model.
cards.next: Run the inspector with SCOUT_MODEL on Binn and review the output.

cards.name: Handling interpretation
cards.desc: Classify the local implementation and summarize it.
cards.summary: HandlingType and InteractionType are coded enums. The heuristic distinguishes local pages from external handoffs; richer types (PDF, form, live feed, API) depend on the model path.
cards.next: Check handling types on real Binn and Ausserberg services.

cards.name: Availability + confidence
cards.desc: How well the municipality supports it, and how sure we are.
cards.summary: Availability enum incl. not_observed, coverage counts per status, and a test that not_observed stays distinct from unavailable. Confidence is carried per service.
cards.next: Calibrate confidence against hand-labelled Binn services.

cards.name: Compile municipality contract
cards.summary: run_scout assembles and validates MunicipalityDiscovery and writes discovery.json, sources.jsonl and crawl-report.json. The fixture and Binn regression suite now pass locally (10/10); a real deterministic Binn run is committed in PR #13.
cards.next: Run the semantic Inspector with a live model on Binn and compare it with the deterministic baseline.

artifacts.name: ScoutFindings[]
artifacts.desc: Candidate services with local label, index relation, confidence and source bundle.
artifacts.summary: ScoutFinding is a Pydantic model with local label, service_id, index relation, confidence and sources. Agent Scrap's ServiceLead (PR #11) is superseded.

artifacts.name: MunicipalityDiscovery JSON
artifacts.desc: The only artifact the MCP Factory needs.
artifacts.summary: municipality-discovery/v1 is a Pydantic model and is produced in the fixture run. A real Binn municipality-discovery/v1 output is committed in PR #13. Factory contract alignment remains an open integration decision.
artifacts.next: Commit a Binn and an Ausserberg discovery.json for the Factory team.

downstream.name: MCP Factory
downstream.desc: Downstream builder. Takes the municipality contract and builds what's next.
downstream.summary: Out of Scout's scope. Two designs are in flight: Patrick's fixed 7-tool server template with generated adapters, and Mark's per-service LLM-generated tools.

layers.name: AI reasoning
layers.note: PydanticAI is now a dependency of pipeline/scout (PR #13). Both agents have deterministic fallbacks and have not yet been run against a live model.

items.name: Reconnaissance interpretation
items.note: The Strategy Agent reads the recon result; recon itself is still deterministic.

items.name: Strategy selection
items.note: PydanticAI Strategy Agent with typed output and heuristic fallback (PR #13).

items.name: Service matching
items.note: Findings matched to Service Index labels and synonyms (PR #13).

items.name: Handling summary
items.note: Service Inspector writes handling summaries; only the heuristic path has run.

items.name: New / variant detection
items.note: possible_new suggestions work; variant is never emitted.

layers.name: Deterministic runtime
layers.note: The model may propose. Software decides what is executable.

items.name: URL safety
items.note: Non-global IPs rejected; every redirect re-validated. Tested on main, PR #7 and PR #11.

items.name: Crawl budgets
items.note: Page and depth limits; truncation reported.

items.name: HTTP / browser escalation
items.note: HTTP only in every codebase. No headless or interactive browser path.

items.name: Snapshots & provenance
items.note: sources.jsonl with hash-based ids and retrieval time (PR #13). Scout does not store raw snapshots yet; Agent Scrap did.

items.name: Schema validation
items.note: Every artifact is a Pydantic model; MunicipalityDiscovery validates on construction (PR #13).

items.name: Stop rules
items.note: Stops on page/depth budget; crawl-report.json records pages and findings but no stop reason.

foundations.name: Contracts (Pydantic models)
foundations.summary: All Scout contracts are Pydantic models: ServiceIndex, ReconResult, ScoutStrategy, ScoutFinding, Handling, MunicipalityService, CatalogSuggestion, CoverageSummary, MunicipalityDiscovery. 2 contract tests pass. Minor: a field named `schema` shadows a BaseModel attribute (warning).
foundations.next: Rename the `schema` field (alias it) to silence the warning.

foundations.name: Provenance
foundations.summary: Source-level provenance (ids, URLs, retrieval time, roles) flows into every MunicipalityService. Raw snapshots are not stored by Scout yet, and handling summaries are not yet marked as interpretation.
foundations.next: Carry source_id + retrieved_at into every MunicipalityService.

foundations.name: Evals & grounding
foundations.summary: Scout metrics are defined, including factory readiness per service. The grounding loop has 1 failing test of 6; nothing has been measured.
foundations.next: Fix idempotency in apply_observations.py; hand-label Binn.

headline.summary: PR #13 builds Scout as a real package: Pydantic contracts, a 5-service index, recon, a PydanticAI strategy agent and service inspector with deterministic fallbacks, source bundles, possible_new suggestions and MunicipalityDiscovery output. 6 of 7 tests pass; the seventh fails on a one-line test bug. Still missing: service_directory and mixed_content, a live-model run, and any committed real municipality output.

open_questions.question: Which contract does the Factory build against: Scout's municipality-discovery/v1 or Patrick's discovery.json? They differ on normalized fields vs. handling summaries, and on not_observed.
Service Index v1 has 5 entries (PR #13); the Factory plan standardizes 7 services. Which list is canonical?
Which Factory design is the team building: Patrick's fixed 7-tool template, or Mark's per-service generated tools?
PydanticAI is in (PR #13). Which model for the first live run — gpt-6-luna now, Apertus as the replacement experiment?
Which strategy family is built second after broad_small_site: service_directory (Dübendorf) or mixed_content (Bosco/Gurin)?
Are action tools (form submission) in scope? Mark's concept has them; Patrick's plan and the Scout docs exclude them.

Align Service Index v1 (5) with the Factory's 7 standard services.
Hand the Factory team one real discovery.json and agree it replaces Patrick's discovery.json shape.

tensions.title: Three discovery contracts
tensions.detail: Scout's municipality-discovery/v1 (handling summaries, not_observed), Patrick's discovery.json (normalized service data, field-level evidence, no not_observed) and Mark's ServiceMention list. The Factory can build against only one.

tensions.title: Three Factory designs
tensions.detail: Patrick: fixed template, same 7 tools everywhere, no runtime LLM, no submissions. Mark: an LLM writes Python tools per service, including action tools that submit forms. Scout docs only say the Factory decides the MCP shape.

tensions.title: Three crawler codebases
tensions.detail: pipeline/prototype (main), pipeline/agent_scrap (PR #11) and pipeline/scout/runtime (PR #13) each implement URL safety, fetching and PageIR. Scout's runtime is the one that matches the design; the others should be retired.

tensions.title: Service Index: 5, 7 or 32
tensions.detail: Scout's index has 5 entries (PR #13), Patrick's Factory plan standardizes 7 services, and the grounding matrix tracks 32 tool hypotheses. Scout checks every index entry, so the list defines coverage.

tensions.title: Observatory edited in two places
tensions.detail: PR #10 edits observatory/index.html, state.json and REFRESH_PROMPT.md on top of the old version; this redesign ships in its own PR. Whichever merges second has to resolve the conflict.

tensions.title: eCH-0070 canonical vs. deferred
tensions.detail: ADR-0001 (accepted) makes eCH-0070 canonical; the Scout build plan explicitly defers universal eCH-0070 mapping.

tensions.title: Strategy mode names
tensions.detail: The docs define broad_small_site, service_directory, targeted_large_city and mixed_content; the code has broad_small_site and a generic targeted.
